remit: underpriced hawkish policy, higher terminal rates, or higher-rate repricing
stance_summary: FACT: the Fed has delivered 25bp to 3.75-4.00% with official SOFR at 3.85, SR3 peaks at 4.735 in 2027-09 then eases, and US labor/services remain expansionary while energy shock-absorbers weaken and BoJ/BoE stay in a tightening-or-split regime. INFERENCE: the strip still prices a completed hike cycle and a shallow post-peak ease that understates inflation persistence. The owned short SOFR_2027-09 remains the clean pay-terminal expression; HOLD rather than add after the already-large 1m front-end rerating.

trade.structure: outright short SOFR_2027-09 (pay implied rate / short duration under the trusted mark convention)
trade.thesis: FACT: policy_paths US overnight SOFR is 3.85 as of 2026-09-17 after jumping from 3.62 on 2026-09-16; the Fed raised 25bp to 3.75-4.00%; SR3 2027-09 implied 4.735 is the strip peak (+88.5bp vs overnight) before 2028-03 4.675 and 2029-06 4.52. FACT: temp:US:inflation 72 with July core PCE +0.2% m/m, ~2.4% 1m/3m and ~3.0% 6m annualized; labor 75 with unemployment 4.1% unchanged, AHE +3.1% y/y, payrolls +162k; activity 69 with ISM services 55.4 and business activity/new orders above 60, GDP +1.5% SAAR in Q2. FACT: August CPI kept the Fed tightening bias intact; BoJ hiked to 1.25%; BoE held 3.75% 6-3 with three votes for 4.00%; energy-market shock absorbers weaken. INFERENCE: a reaction function that still cares about above-target 6m PCE, a non-breaking labor market, and a global energy/tightening overlay will not treat 4.735 as a durable terminal or validate the ~21bp post-peak ease. Paying the peak SR3 contract owns extra hikes and delayed easing in one liquid mark. UNKNOWN: the next FOMC statement path beyond the delivered hike, full August CPI components, and CFTC crowding.
trade.mispricing: FACT: SR3 prices ~88.5bp of additional tightening from SOFR 3.85 to a 4.735 peak, then a gentle fade. INFERENCE: that path assumes the September hike plus about three more 25bp steps completes the cycle and that inflation/labor cool enough to allow modest easing into 2028-29. The hawk disagreement is that persistence, services strength, and the energy/global-tightening overlay keep the terminal higher and keep the easing tail from being earned. UNKNOWN: whether the residual 21bp of post-peak ease is the larger error than the level of the peak itself.
why_now: FACT: the 25bp hike is now realized (SOFR 3.85 on 2026-09-17) after >90% pre-decision pricing, so the live debate has shifted from the September meeting to the terminal and pause.
FACT: August CPI was already in the tape as keeping the tightening bias, and last-24h BoJ 1.25% plus BoE 6-3 hike dissent keep global easing constrained.
INFERENCE: that is when underpriced extra restriction shows up in the 2027 peak contract rather than in the front 1m SOFR, which already embeds the delivered hike.
evidence_refs: rollup:August CPI keeps the Fed tightening bias intact
last24:BoJ raises its policy rate to 1.25%
last24:BoE holds 3.75%, but three members vote to hike
trade.horizon: 3-6 months, through the 2027 peak of the SR3 strip
trade.invalidation: Thesis is wrong if SR3 2027-09 implied rate moves lower because the strip prices a peak below the current 4.735 while US labor breaks from unemployment 4.1% and ISM services/new orders lose expansion, or if post-hike Fed communication treats 3.75-4.00% as terminal while 6m core PCE cools through the observed ~2.4% 1m/3m pace.
catalysts: Further US inflation prints that keep the tightening bias after the delivered hike
Labor/services data that refuse to break (payrolls, unemployment, ISM services/new orders)
Energy pass-through and weaker shock-absorbers spilling into US and global reaction functions
BoJ/BoE-style tightening or hawkish splits reinforcing that global easing is constrained
principal_risks: FACT: US 2Y 4.76 / 5Y 4.86 / 10Y 5.01 already sit at ~99th 1y percentiles after +57bp/+51bp/+36bp over 1m, so a large hawkish rerating is already in the price.
FACT: Q2 GDP decelerated to +1.5% SAAR and Michigan preliminary September sentiment fell to 47.8; a demand break would validate the priced easing tail.
UNKNOWN: CFTC positioning is null, so crowding of the pay-terminal view cannot be measured.
INFERENCE: if the September hike was the last step markets needed, paying 4.735 is negative carry versus overnight SOFR 3.85.

context_build.causal_mechanism: FACT: US inflation remains above a policy-neutral pace on 6m core PCE (~3.0% annualized) with unemployment 4.1% unchanged and ISM services in expansion. INFERENCE: the Fed reaction function that just hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% will not quickly pivot if those conditions persist, especially with energy shock-absorbers weakening and BoJ/BoE still resisting easing. The mechanism being tested is inflation persistence plus a still-restrictive reaction function, not a claim that nothing is priced.
context_build.path_to_current_price: FACT: official SOFR held near 3.5-3.7 from May through 2026-09-16 then printed 3.85 on 2026-09-17 after the 25bp hike. US 2Y is 4.76 (+9bp 1d, +13bp 5d, +57bp 1m); 5Y 4.86 (+8bp 1d, +8bp 5d, +51bp 1m); 10Y 5.01 (+7bp 1d, +5bp 5d, +36bp 1m). SR3 strip: 2026-09 4.00, 2026-12 4.315, 2027-03 4.565, 2027-06 4.70, 2027-09 4.735 peak, then 2027-12 4.71 through 2029-06 4.52. Paper_books mark the owned SOFR_2027-09 short at 4.755 with sidecar entry_mark 4.75. INFERENCE: the path here is a delivered, pre-priced hike plus a still-steep near-term hiking path, not a surprise tightening shock.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: FACT known before the cutoff: Reuters 2026-09-16 noted >90% odds of the 25bp hike; August CPI (Sep 11) kept the tightening bias; labor/PCE/ISM prints were already in the gauges. FACT new or newly realized: the hike is delivered and SOFR printed 3.85; BoJ raised to 1.25%; BoE held 6-3 with three votes for a hike and gilt QT; energy shock-absorbers weaken; desk thesis that global tightening plus the energy shock constrains easing. INFERENCE: the September hike itself does not justify a new long-duration pay, but the post-decision terminal/pause debate plus the global overlay does justify keeping the existing pay of the 2027-09 peak.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: FACT: from SOFR 3.85 the SR3 curve prices about 88.5bp of extra tightening to a 4.735 peak in 2027-09 and then about 21.5bp of easing to 4.52 by 2029-06. INFERENCE: the market's required assumption is that the tightening cycle completes near 4.75 and that inflation/labor cool enough for a shallow ease thereafter. 1m SOFR already shows Oct 3.91 / Dec 4.1975, so the next steps are not unpriced.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: INFERENCE: the hawk disagrees that 4.735 is a sufficient terminal and that the post-peak fade is earned. Persistence in 6m PCE, a labor market that is not breaking, services new orders above 60, and an energy/global-tightening overlay imply a higher peak and/or no ease. FACT: this is not a claim that zero hikes are priced.
context_build.price_decomposition: FACT: level vs change — US 2Y/5Y/10Y are already 99th-percentile 1y levels, but the 1m change is front-loaded (2Y +57bp, 5Y +51bp, 10Y +36bp) and 2s10s is 25bp at the 0.2nd 1y percentile. STIR decomposition: overnight 3.85; 1m strip climbs to 4.695 by 2027-08; 3m peak 4.735 in 2027-09; beyond that the curve is a shallow downslope. INFERENCE: the marginal driver is still the policy-path peak, not 10Y term premium. Paper mid for the owned contract is 4.755 in paper_books versus 4.735 implied in policy_paths; UNKNOWN which mid trusted code will use, so no authored entry.

historical_reference.distribution: FACT: US 2Y 4.76 is 99.8th 1y / 88.0th 5y; 5Y 4.86 is 99.6th 1y and 5y; 10Y 5.01 is 99.6th 1y / 99.9th 5y; 2s10s 25bp is 0.2nd 1y / 54th 5y. Those percentiles are discovery flags that a lot of tightening is already in sovereign yields, not proof the STIR terminal is high enough.
analogs: 2023 US skip-then-hike: markets repeatedly priced a pause after a delivered hike while inflation and labor had not broken, then the path repriced higher.
2022-24 higher-for-longer versus repeated front-end easing: inflation persistence kept terminals above the first post-hike strip peak even after activity decelerated.
historical_reference.regime_differences: FACT: today's funds band is 3.75-4.00% with 6m core PCE near 3.0%, unemployment 4.1%, and Q2 GDP already +1.5% SAAR — not the 2022 5%+ inflation / 5.25-5.50% funds starting point. Energy-shock overlay and BoJ at a 31-year high are structural differences versus a clean 2023 disinflation analog. INFERENCE: analogs support persistence after a hike, not a mechanical replay of 2022 hiking amplitude.

policy_path_check.rationale: Short-end US policy pricing is present and is the right starting point before sovereign 2Y/5Y/10Y. The hawk discrepancy lives in the US peak/easing tail (4.735 then fade), not in Canada where 136bp of hikes are already priced against CPI-trim/median at 1.9/2.0% and wages/employment cooling, nor in Australia where only ~60bp more is priced but housing volumes/stamp duty are already contracting and AU 2Y/5Y/10Y are 99th percentile.

stir_policy_path.rationale: FACT: SR3 2027-09 at 4.735 is the observable US terminal/peak, +88.5bp vs SOFR 3.85, then the strip eases. That is the cleanest markable expression of underpriced extra hikes or delayed easing. CA CORRA and AU AONIA are inferior: Canada already prices ~136bp of hikes with core at target and labor weakening; Australia prices ~60bp more but housing is biting and AONIA liquidity thins past the front months.

two_year.rationale: FACT: US 2Y 4.76, +57bp 1m, 99.8th 1y / 88th 5y, close to the SR3 peak. Paying 2Y is a valid higher-front-end expression, but a 2Y percentile is not a substitute for the policy path and the 1m rerating is already extreme.

five_year.rationale: FACT: US 5Y 4.86, +51bp 1m, 99.6th 1y and 5y. It can pay if the hiking cycle extends through 2027, but it mixes term premium with policy and is already at a historical extreme.

ten_year.rationale: FACT: US 10Y 5.01, 99.6th 1y / 99.9th 5y, only +36bp 1m. The hawk view is a reaction-function/terminal argument, not a 10Y duration or term-premium argument; this tenor is the wrong owner and already stretched.

curve.rationale: FACT: US 2s10s 25bp at 0.2nd 1y percentile (-21bp 1m). Extra hikes would flatten further, delayed easing can steepen, and the curve is already at a 1y extreme. Mixed hawk implications plus no room as a flattener make curve a poor expression.

cross_market_rv.rationale: FACT: CA-US 2Y -140bp at 3.8th 1y / 4.3rd 5y; CA-US 5Y -124bp at 0.2nd 1y. Paying US versus Canada is already an extreme. BoC minutes flag energy pass-through, which would reprice CORRA higher and compress the spread. NZ RV is unavailable (RBNZ B2 403). AU-US 2Y +26bp is not a 1y extreme.

rates_tenor_scan.selection_rationale: The discrepancy is the US policy-path peak and the unearned easing tail after a delivered hike. SOFR_2027-09 is the liquid SR3 contract at that peak. 2Y/5Y are valid but already 99th-percentile sovereigns and are not substitutes for the strip. Curve and CA-US RV fight already-extreme levels and mixed country residuals.

rates_candidate.rationale: Pay the SR3 2027-09 peak (short duration / profits if implied rate rises). This is the selected stir_policy_path bucket and matches the owned book instrument.

expression_comparison.rationale: Rates are cleaner: the mispricing is the US terminal/easing tail, which SR3 owns directly. USDCAD would mix a 140bp CA-US 2Y gap, a BoC hiking cycle already priced at ~136bp, and energy terms-of-trade for CAD. USDCHF is already 99.8th 1y. Prefer rates when both expressions are usable; here rates are strictly cleaner and the seat already owns the SR3 contract.

conflict_synopsis.core_view: After a delivered 25bp hike, SR3 still peaks at 4.735 and then eases; inflation persistence, non-breaking labor/services, and a global energy/tightening overlay leave that terminal and easing tail too low.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Post-hike US inflation/labor/services prints and energy/global-tightening spillovers that force a higher SR3 peak.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: SR3 2027-09 implied rate falls as the strip prices a peak below 4.735 while US labor and services break.
